title: Ichthyosis vulgaris: defective keratinocyte desquamation (filaggrin)
vignette: A 26-year-old woman comes to the office due to a skin condition. The patient has had dry, flaky skin since childhood, but it has worsened in recent years. Symptoms are typically worse in the winter but improve as the weather warms in the spring. The patient has a family history of asthma; both parents also have chronically dry skin. Examination shows diffuse scaling of the skin that is most notable on the extremities, with fish-scale-like plaques on the shins. Which of the following is most likely contributing to this patient's condition?

clues.note: Lifelong dry, scaly skin points to an inherited disorder of cornification (ichthyosis) rather than an acquired dermatitis.

clues.text: worse in the winter but improve as the weather warms
clues.note: Seasonal worsening with low winter humidity is characteristic of ichthyosis vulgaris (and dry-skin disorders in general).

clues.text: family history of asthma; both parents also have chronically dry skin
clues.note: A family history of atopy (asthma) plus inherited dry skin fits ichthyosis vulgaris, which is caused by filaggrin gene mutations and overlaps with atopic disease.

clues.text: diffuse scaling of the skin that is most notable on the extremities
clues.note: Diffuse scaling that spares the flexures and is most prominent on the extensor surfaces/extremities is the classic distribution of ichthyosis vulgaris.

whatMatters: Lifelong dry, fish-scale skin, worse in winter, with a family/atopy history = ichthyosis vulgaris, caused by FILAGGRIN gene mutations. Filaggrin normally aggregates keratin and supports the epidermal barrier and normal shedding; its loss causes DEFECTIVE KERATINOCYTE DESQUAMATION with retained corneocytes (scaling). Answer C.
strategy: Recognize ichthyosis vulgaris (inherited, lifelong, extensor scaling, winter-worse, atopy-linked filaggrin defect), then name the defect: retention hyperkeratosis from impaired keratinocyte desquamation. Reject other skin mechanisms: androgen/sebum (acne), anti-desmoglein antibodies (pemphigus), collagen deposition (scleroderma), and T-cell reaction (contact dermatitis).

eliminations.label: Androgen-induced sebum - acne vulgaris
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: increased sebum from androgen drive causes acne vulgaris (comedones, papules, pustules). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: diffuse dry scaling is the opposite of oily acne. ✅ Correct if: adolescent inflammatory acne.

eliminations.label: Anti-desmoglein antibodies - pemphigus vulgaris
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: autoantibodies against desmogleins 1/3 cause acantholysis and flaccid bullae (pemphigus vulgaris). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: pemphigus makes fragile blisters/erosions, not lifelong fish-scale dryness. ✅ Correct if: flaccid bullae that rupture into erosions (positive Nikolsky).

eliminations.label: Excessive collagen - systemic sclerosis
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: excess dermal collagen deposition causes skin thickening/hardening (scleroderma). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: that's tight, indurated skin, not dry scaling. ✅ Correct if: sclerodactyly/skin tightening with Raynaud and fingertip ulcers.

eliminations.label: T-cell-mediated reaction - allergic contact dermatitis
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a type IV reaction to allergens (e.g., poison ivy) causing a localized pruritic vesicular rash. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it's acute and localized to exposure sites, not a lifelong diffuse scaling disorder. ✅ Correct if: a delayed vesicular rash after allergen contact.

reasoning: Lifelong dry, fish-scale skin, winter-worse, with an atopy/family history = ichthyosis vulgaris
Ichthyosis vulgaris is caused by filaggrin gene mutations
Loss of filaggrin impairs keratin aggregation and normal shedding -> retained corneocytes
mechanism: Ichthyosis vulgaris is the most common inherited disorder of cornification, caused by mutations in the FILAGGRIN gene. Filaggrin normally aggregates keratin filaments in the stratum corneum and contributes to the skin barrier and natural moisturizing factor; its deficiency produces epidermal hyperplasia with DEFECTIVE keratinocyte desquamation (retention hyperkeratosis), so corneocytes accumulate as dry, fish-scale-like scaling. It typically involves the trunk and the EXTENSOR surfaces of the extremities (sparing the flexures and face), begins in childhood, and worsens in winter (low humidity). Filaggrin mutations also predispose to atopic disease (eczema, asthma), explaining the family history here. The distractors describe unrelated mechanisms: androgen/sebum (acne), anti-desmoglein antibodies (pemphigus), collagen deposition (systemic sclerosis), and a T-cell reaction (allergic contact dermatitis).
